description: Report cites one real, gold-relevant transaction alongside one fabricated id that doesn't exist in the case.
report_text: N100 sent funds to M201 (T1-001), corroborated by T3-999.
flag: Precision/recall/F1 all read as a PERFECT 1.0 here, despite the report citing a fabricated id. This is because ComputeTraceability's precision denominator is 'grounded' citations (cited AND real), which excludes fabricated citations entirely -- fabrication is invisible to the traceability metric itself. It is only visible via the separate fabricated_citations list/count (and, upstream, via EGHR's deterministic backstop on the *claim* that cited it). A policy or report that looks only at traceability precision/recall/F1 without also checking fabricated_citation_count would never notice this report fabricated evidence. This is a real, testable definitional interaction worth surfacing, not a bug in the traceability math itself -- precision/recall genuinely are about the *real* citations only; fabrication is a distinct, separately-tracked concern by design. But it means 'high traceability score' must never be read alone as 'no fabrication' without also checking fabricated_citation_count.
